correctness.rationale: The claim is reconstructed from the six ball inequalities. They reduce to \(\lVert x\rVert^2+\sqrt2\lVert x\rVert_\infty\le1/2\), which gives the eight vertices exactly. Edge geometry gives \(\cos\alpha=23/27\); spherical Gauss--Bonnet gives each face area \(2(\pi-5\alpha)/3\); the divergence theorem plus an explicit boundary vector-area integral gives the volume; and the standard smooth-face plus edge-curvature formula gives the mean width. The packaged verifier checks the exact identities and independently reproduces the volume by radial quadrature. The numerical computation is supplemental and no finite experiment is used to infer an infinite statement.

originality.rationale: Finch (arXiv:1301.5515v1) explicitly poses the exact volume, surface-area, and mean-width evaluation of this same six-ball spherical hexahedron as unanswered. Targeted statement, alias, constant, and broader-method searches found no source stating these closed forms. The 2015 six-sphere paper inspected in full text treats coplanar regular-hexagon centers, not the octahedral centers here. Dodd--Theodorou gives a general volume/surface-area algorithm but no inspected statement of these closed forms and no mean-width result. Lustig (1985) is a genuine residual risk because the full text was inaccessible; that access gap is recorded rather than treated as novelty evidence.

value.rationale: The result answers an explicit published three-part exact-evaluation question for a canonical octahedrally symmetric ball polyhedron. It supplies all three intrinsic measures requested, an exact edge/face geometry, and corrects the adjacent-vertex normalization needed to reconcile the source equations with its numerical volume ratio. This is a natural complete evaluation of the named object, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of a known table.
